title: PSKH1 kinase activity is differentially modulated via allosteric binding of Ca2+ sensor proteins
projectDescription: Protein Serine Kinase H1 (PSKH1) was recently identified as a crucial factor in kidney development and is overexpressed in prostate, lung and kidney cancers. However, little is known about PSKH1’s regulation, leading to its classification as a “dark” kinase. Here, we used biochemistry and mass spectrometry to define PSKH1’s consensus substrate motif, protein interactors, and how interactors, including Ca2+ sensor proteins, promote or suppress activity.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Initially, we C-terminally tagged PSKH1 with the TurboID variant of BirA, to facilitate rapid promiscuous biotinylation of proteins proximal to PSKH1 upon induction of its expression with doxycycline in HEL cells. Proteins were enriched following Streptavidin immunoprecipitation, tryptic digest and mass spectrometry analysis via DIA-MS on a timsTOF Pro MS. We next validated these interactions using the orthogonal proteomics methods including BiCAP. BiCAP involves C-terminal fusion of PSKH1 with a split Venus, which when dimerized can be immunoprecipitated by GFP Trap enrichment. BiCAP samples were subjected to FASP digestion and subsequent DIA-MS acquisition on a timsTOF Pro MS.
dataProcessingProtocol: DIA data were analysed using DIA-NN 1.8.1 in library-free mode. Bruker diaPASEF d. files were searched against reviewed sequences from human Uniprot Reference Proteome (downloaded May 2021). Data processing and analysis were performed using R (version 4.1.2).
keywords: Protein kinase; allosteric regulation; calumenin; erc-55; cab-45
